text:
hina: quick sync: i prototyped separating score computation from ranking in the policy engine. idea is to compute a canonical "route_score" asynchronously and let the matcher only read stable values. want quick feedback on tradeoffs.

leo: sounds promising. main win is cheaper per-request compute. worry: staleness windows could cause oscillation when routing reacts slower.

dana: would like to see how penalties for tier preemption fit in. we still need to ensure enterprise SLOs don't get preempted by smaller noisy tenants.

hina: current sketch: compute base_cost from perf telemetry, then apply tier_penalty and preemptive_shim as separate additive terms. the sequencer then sorts by (base_cost + tier_penalty + shim). precompute runs every 300ms for hot routes.

mike: paste pseudocode pls.

hina: sure:
```
base = calc_base_cost(route_metrics)
penalty = if tenant_tier=="gold" then 0 else tier_map[tenant_tier]
shim = preemptive_bias(route_state)
route_score = base + penalty + shim
store(route_key, {score: route_score, last_seen: now})
```

leo: what's preemptive_bias? is it dynamic per-tenant?

hina: preemptive_bias is small dynamic value to pull traffic off nodes that are nearing soft-preempt threshold. computed from lease_utilization and recent preempt_events. bounded to avoid large swings.

dana: migration concern: old policies expect ranking to be immediate. if score store is opt-in, ok. but need fallback: on cache-miss compute on-path.

hina: agreed. default behavior: on cache-miss compute synchronously then warm the store. Also add a stale_allowed window to allow using older score up to X ms.

mike: what about debugging and explainability? ops will want per-decision breakdown.

hina: plan: attach score breakdown metadata with each decision: base/penalty/shim/timestamp. expose in trace & console. Also add an audit flag when stale_used==true.

leo: perf: precompute frequency * hot route count => CPU. propose tiered schedule: hot 200ms, warm 1s, cold on-request. plus leader election to avoid duplicate work across hosts.

dana: leader election ok but add fallback: if no leader writes store, any host can compute on-demand.

hina: policy surface changes: add optional fields: score_ttl_ms, precompute_class (auto/hot/warm/cold), allow_stale_ms. safe defaults chosen.

mike: tests: unit math + integration sim with 10k routes, induce sudden spikes and verify 95p traffic shift < 1s for hot routes. chaos: kill metric feed and verify preemptive_bias pushes traffic away gradually.

deploy-bot: canary rollout created: rollout/score-decouple-2026-03-21 -> 3% dedicated us-east1

hina: thanks all. i'll write RFC with perf numbers, console UX mockups, and a migration guide. tagging @eng-runtime for review.
